hints: Look at how many moles of HCl each calcium compound can neutralise, they all need 2 moles of HCl per 1 mole of Y.
If 100 moles of HCl are neutralised, you must have used exactly 50 moles of Y, so work out what mass one mole must have.
Divide the total mass in grams by 50 moles to get the $M_r$ of Y, then see which formula matches that value.
walkthrough:
**Find the mole ratio with HCl**

All four possible substances react with HCl in a 1 to 2 ratio. One mole of Y neutralises two moles of HCl.

$$\text{Ca} + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2$$
$$\text{CaO} + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Find moles and $M_r$ of Y**

To neutralise 100 moles of HCl, you need half as many moles of Y.

$$n(\text{Y}) = 100 / 2 = 50 \text{ mol}$$

**Calculate the required molar mass**

Convert the mass to grams, then use mass divided by moles.

$$m(\text{Y}) = 3.705 \text{ kg} = 3705 \text{ g}$$
$$M_r(\text{Y}) = 3705 / 50 = 74.1$$

**Match $M_r$ to the options**

Now calculate $M_r$ for $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ using $\text{Ca}=40.1$, $\text{O}=16.0$, $\text{H}=1.0$.

$$M_r = 40.1 + 2 \times (16.0 + 1.0) = 74.1$$

**Conclude the identity**

The required $M_r$ of 74.1 matches $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ exactly, so substance Y must be calcium hydroxide.

options.A: Ca reacts 1:2 with HCl, so 50 mol are needed. Mass would be $50 \times 40.1 = 2005$ g (2.005 kg), which is much too light compared to 3.705 kg.
options.B: CaO reacts 1:2 with HCl, so 50 mol are needed. With $M_r = 56.1$, mass would be $50 \times 56.1 = 2805$ g (2.805 kg), which is less than 3.705 kg.
options.C: Ca(OH)2 reacts 1:2 with HCl, so 50 mol are needed. With $M_r = 74.1$, mass is $50 \times 74.1 = 3705$ g = 3.705 kg, which matches the data exactly.
options.D: CaCO3 reacts 1:2 with HCl, so 50 mol are needed. With $M_r = 100.1$, mass would be $50 \times 100.1 = 5005$ g (5.005 kg), which is too heavy.
